query: In Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs phase stability and why, with relevance to retaining desirable combinations of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness? Specify a controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to a baseline, the boundaries of the hypothesis, supporting prior evidence, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys, the valence electron concentration (VEC) controls the relative electronic free energy of FCC versus BCC lattices: when VEC falls below a critical threshold (~7.8), the electronic band filling destabilizes FCC and stabilizes BCC, driving a phase transition. This electronic mechanism governs phase stability and thereby impacts high-temperature strength, corrosion resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted, homogenized Al_x(CoCrFeNi)_1–x alloys with x=0.1 (VEC≈8.13) and x=0.3 (VEC≈7.47).
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of Al content from x=0.1 to x=0.3 to cross the predicted VEC threshold.
generation.conditions: Isothermal anneal at 800 °C for 24 h followed by furnace cooling to room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Volume fractions of FCC and BCC phases measured by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD).
generation.mechanism: Changing Al content alters VEC and thus band filling; lower VEC raises the electronic free energy of FCC relative to BCC, favoring BCC nucleation and growth.
generation.predicted_outcome: Alloy at x=0.1 will be >95% FCC; alloy at x=0.3 will show ≥30% BCC fraction, relative to the x=0.1 baseline.
generation.baseline: Al_0.1(CoCrFeNi)_0.9 (VEC≈8.13), expected to form a single-phase FCC.
generation.boundary: Valid for 0.05≤x(Al)≤0.35 (VEC≈7.4–8.3), annealing T between 600–900 °C, furnace-cooled, no additional principal elements or extreme quench rates.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—atomic size mismatch and enthalpy of mixing may modulate the effect; predicted phase fractions ±10%.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize Al_0.1 and Al_0.3(CoCrFeNi) alloys, anneal at 800 °C/24 h furnace-cool, then characterize phase fractions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If both compositions exhibit >90% FCC or if BCC fraction does not increase systematically as VEC decreases, the hypothesis is falsified.
